
# DEGs

## T-Test Function

```{r}
# Function to calculate Fold Change and P-value for a specific virus vs Mock at a given timepoint
# (timepoint defaults to "24h" so existing calls keep the same behaviour)
run_deg_analysis <- function(data_matrix, target_virus, timepoint = "24h") {

  # Identify column indices for the target virus and the mock control at the same timepoint
  idx_virus <- grep(paste0("^", target_virus, "_", timepoint, "_"), colnames(data_matrix))
  idx_mock <- grep(paste0("^mock_", timepoint, "_"), colnames(data_matrix))
  
  # Apply t-test row by row (gene by gene)
  results <- t(apply(data_matrix, 1, function(gene_expr) {
    expr_virus <- gene_expr[idx_virus]
    expr_mock <- gene_expr[idx_mock]
    
    # Calculate log2 Fold Change (mean of virus minus mean of mock)
    # Since data is already log2 transformed: log2(A) - log2(B) = log2(A/B)
    logFC <- mean(expr_virus) - mean(expr_mock)
    
    # Run t-test (suppress errors if variance is 0)
    p_val <- tryCatch(
      t.test(expr_virus, expr_mock, var.equal = TRUE)$p.value,
      error = function(e) NA
    )
    
    return(c(logFC = logFC, pvalue = p_val))
  }))
  
  # Convert to dataframe
  res_df <- as.data.frame(results)
  res_df$Gene <- rownames(res_df)
  
  # Apply Multiple Testing Correction (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR)
  res_df$padj <- p.adjust(res_df$pvalue, method = "BH")
  
  return(res_df)
}
```

## Run T-Tests for each virus

```{r}
# Run the analysis for each virus vs Mock at 24h
deg_H7N9 <- run_deg_analysis(data_log, "H7N9")
deg_H3N2 <- run_deg_analysis(data_log, "H3N2")
deg_H7N7 <- run_deg_analysis(data_log, "H7N7")
deg_VN1203 <- run_deg_analysis(data_log, "VN1203")

# Check the top most significant genes for H7N9
head(deg_H7N9[order(deg_H7N9$padj), ])
```

## Significant dysregulated genes

```{r}
# Count how many DEGs each virus triggered at 24h, up or downregulated by more than double or half
sig_threshold <- function(df) {
  sum(df$padj < 0.05 & abs(df$logFC) > 1, na.rm = TRUE)
}

cat("Significant DEGs at 24h:\n",
    "H7N9: ", sig_threshold(deg_H7N9), "\n",
    "H3N2: ", sig_threshold(deg_H3N2), "\n",
    "H7N7: ", sig_threshold(deg_H7N7), "\n",
    "VN1203: ", sig_threshold(deg_VN1203), "\n")
```

## Venn Diagrams for DEGs

```{r}
# Extract significant upregulated and downregulated genes
get_up_genes <- function(df) df[which(df$padj < 0.05 & df$logFC > 1), "Gene"]
get_down_genes <- function(df) df[which(df$padj < 0.05 & df$logFC < -1), "Gene"]

list_UP <- list(
  H3N2   = get_up_genes(deg_H3N2),
  H7N7   = get_up_genes(deg_H7N7),
  H7N9   = get_up_genes(deg_H7N9),
  VN1203 = get_up_genes(deg_VN1203)
)

list_DOWN <- list(
  H3N2   = get_down_genes(deg_H3N2),
  H7N7   = get_down_genes(deg_H7N7),
  H7N9   = get_down_genes(deg_H7N9),
  VN1203 = get_down_genes(deg_VN1203)
)

# Plot Upregulated DEGs intersection
plot_UP <- ggVennDiagram(list_UP, label_alpha = 0, set_size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F4FAFE", high = "#E41A1C") +
  labs(title = "Upregulated Genes at 24h", subtitle = "padj < 0.05, log2FC > 1") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Plot Downregulated DEGs intersection
plot_DOWN <- ggVennDiagram(list_DOWN, label_alpha = 0, set_size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F4FAFE", high = "#377EB8") +
  labs(title = "Downregulated Genes at 24h", subtitle = "padj < 0.05, log2FC < -1") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

plot_UP
plot_DOWN
```

## Heatmap targeted on H7N9 dysregulated genes

```{r}
# 1. Combine the unique up and down genes into one list
h7n9_exclusive_genes <- c(unique_up_H7N9, unique_down_H7N9)

# 2. Subset the main log2 normalized matrix to keep only these genes
# We isolate only the 24h samples to keep the visual clean and focused
idx_24h <- grep("_24h", colnames(data_log))
matrix_24h <- data_log[h7n9_exclusive_genes, idx_24h]

# 3. Scale the data by row (gene) to highlight relative differences across viruses
# This centers each gene around 0, making patterns instantly visible
matrix_scaled <- t(scale(t(matrix_24h)))

# 4. Create annotation dataframe for the top of the heatmap
annotation_col <- data.frame(
  Virus = sapply(strsplit(colnames(matrix_24h), "_"), `[`, 1)
)
rownames(annotation_col) <- colnames(matrix_24h)

# Define matching colors for the annotation
ann_colors <- list(
  Virus = c(H3N2 = "#377EB8", H7N7 = "#FF7F00", 
            H7N9 = "#984EA3", mock = "#E41A1C", VN1203 = "#4DAF4A")
)

# 5. Generate the heatmap
pheatmap(matrix_scaled, 
         cluster_cols = TRUE,    # Cluster samples based on expression similarity
         cluster_rows = FALSE,    # Cluster genes with similar patterns
         show_rownames = FALSE,  # Hide 2,000+ gene names to keep it readable
         annotation_col = annotation_col,
         annotation_colors = ann_colors,
         color = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "firebrick3"))(50),
         main = "Expression Profile of H7N9-Exclusive DEGs at 24h",
         fontsize_col = 8)
```

# Heatmaps : Is one virus different from the others?

Three complementary heatmaps, with hierarchical clustering of the columns. If a virus stands out, its columns form a separate branch of the dendrogram.

1.  **Samples, one time point at a time**: z-score per gene, UP and DOWN genes kept in separate blocks.
2.  **log2FC of the 16 comparisons**: no z-score, because the sign and magnitude of the log2FC are meaningful.
3.  **Correlation between the 16 signatures**: Pearson correlation of the log2FC values.

```{r}
library(pheatmap)

# save in png
save_ph <- function(ph, file, width = 8, height = 8) {
  png(file, width = width, height = height, units = "in", res = 300)
  grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(ph$gtable)
  dev.off()
}

# Colours : red = UP, blue = DOWN, white = 0
pal <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100)

# Colours (virus and time)
ann_colors <- list(
  virus = cols_virus,
  time  = setNames(c("#EEEEEE", "#BBBBBB", "#777777", "#333333"), times)
)

n_top <- 1000   # Maximum number of genes displayed (the most variable ones) for readability
```

```{r}
# --- 1. Heatmap of samples, one time point at a time -------------------------
# Rows = DEG (detected in at least one virus at this time point), columns = samples from this time point (including mock)
# Values = z-score per gene: (expression - mean for the gene) / standard deviation
#   -> we compare the PROFILES of the genes across samples, not their absolute levels
for (t in times) {
  genes_t <- unique(unlist(deg[paste0(viruses, "_", t)]))
  samp_t  <- meta$sample[meta$time == t]
  mat <- logexpr[genes_t, samp_t]
  mat <- mat[apply(mat, 1, var) > 0, ]                       # removes constant genes
  mat <- mat[head(order(apply(mat, 1, var), decreasing = TRUE), n_top), ]
  z   <- t(scale(t(mat)))                                    # z-score BY GENE (per row)
  
  # Gene direction = sign of its average log2FC across the 4 viruses at this time point
  #   average > 0 -> UP (upregulated by infection), average < 0 -> DOWN
  lfc_t <- sapply(viruses, function(v) {
    r <- res[[paste(v, t, sep = "_")]]
    r$log2FC[match(rownames(z), r$gene)]
  })
  up_t <- rownames(z)[rowMeans(lfc_t) >  0]
  dn_t <- rownames(z)[rowMeans(lfc_t) <= 0]
  
  # We organise the genes: the UP block at the top, the DOWN block at the bottom.
  # Within each block, we group together genes with similar profiles
  # (without ever moving a gene from one block to the other)
  clust_block <- function(g) if (length(g) > 2) g[hclust(dist(z[g, ]))$order] else g
  z <- z[c(clust_block(up_t), clust_block(dn_t)), ]
  
  ann     <- data.frame(virus = meta$virus[meta$time == t], row.names = samp_t)
  ann_row <- data.frame(Sens = rep(c("UP", "DOWN"), c(length(up_t), length(dn_t))),
                        row.names = rownames(z))
  
  ph <- pheatmap(z, color = pal, breaks = seq(-3, 3, length.out = 101),
                 cluster_cols = TRUE,
                 cluster_rows = FALSE,             # keep the order: UP at the top, DOWN at the bottom
                 gaps_row = length(up_t),          # white line between UP and DOWN
                 show_rownames = FALSE, annotation_col = ann,
                 annotation_row = ann_row,         # UP / DOWN on the left
                 annotation_colors = c(ann_colors["virus"],
                                       list(Sens = c(UP = "red", DOWN = "blue"))),
                 main = paste0("Samples at ", t, " - ", length(up_t), " UP / ",
                               length(dn_t), " DOWN (z-score)"))
  save_ph(ph, paste0("figures/06_heatmap_samples_", t, ".png"), width = 8, height = 7)
}
```

```{r}
# --- 2. Heatmap of log2FC values for the 16 comparisons --------------------------------
# Rows = DEGs in at least one comparison; columns = virus_time
# Values = log2FC vs mock (no z-score: the sign and magnitude are meaningful)
lfc <- sapply(res, function(d) d$log2FC)
rownames(lfc) <- res[[1]]$gene
all_deg <- unique(unlist(deg))
lfc_deg <- lfc[all_deg, ]
lfc_deg <- lfc_deg[head(order(apply(lfc_deg, 1, var), decreasing = TRUE), n_top), ]

ann_comp <- data.frame(virus = sub("_.*", "", colnames(lfc)),
                       time  = sub(".*_", "", colnames(lfc)),
                       row.names = colnames(lfc))

ph_lfc <- pheatmap(lfc_deg, color = pal, breaks = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 101),
                   cluster_cols = TRUE, cluster_rows = TRUE,
                   show_rownames = FALSE, annotation_col = ann_comp,
                   annotation_colors = ann_colors,
                   main = paste0("log2FC vs mock - ", nrow(lfc_deg), " the most variable genes"))
save_ph(ph_lfc, "figures/07_heatmap_log2FC_all.png", width = 9, height = 9)
```

```{r}
# --- 3. Correlation between the 16 signatures -----------------------------------
# Pearson's correlation of log2FC values (across all DEGs)
# Close to 1 = both viruses modulate the same genes in the same direction
cor_lfc <- cor(lfc[all_deg, ], method = "pearson")

ph_cor <- pheatmap(cor_lfc, color = colorRampPalette(c("white", "#FDB863", "#B2182B"))(100),
                   breaks = seq(0, 1, length.out = 101),
                   cluster_cols = TRUE, cluster_rows = TRUE,
                   display_numbers = TRUE, number_format = "%.2f", fontsize_number = 7,
                   annotation_col = ann_comp, annotation_row = ann_comp,
                   annotation_colors = ann_colors,
                   main = "Correlation of log2FC values across comparisons")
save_ph(ph_cor, "figures/08_heatmap_correlation.png", width = 10, height = 9)

# Table: Correlation between H7N9 and each other virus, at the same time
cor_h7n9 <- sapply(times, function(t)
  sapply(setdiff(viruses, "H7N9"), function(v)
    cor_lfc[paste0("H7N9_", t), paste0(v, "_", t)]))
round(cor_h7n9, 2)
```

```{r}
# 2. Run Reactome Enrichment Analysis (Relaxing the UP cutoff to see trends)
reactome_up <- enrichPathway(gene = genes_up_entrez$ENTREZID,

                               organism = "human", 
                               pvalueCutoff = 0.05, 
                               readable = TRUE)

# 3. Visualize Top Pathways (Adding label_format to wrap long text)
dotplot(reactome_up, showCategory = 15, 
        title = "Reactome: Upregulated in H7N9 (Exclusive)", 
        label_format = 40)

dotplot(reactome_down, showCategory = 15, 
        title = "Reactome: Downregulated in H7N9 (Exclusive)",
```

### EnrichR (GO, KEGG)

```{r}
# 1. Define the reference databases to capture a multi-dimensional biological profile:
# - GO Biological Process (BP): Identifies the overarching systemic responses (e.g., immune evasion, cell death).
# - GO Molecular Function (MF): Highlights the specific biochemical activities of the dysregulated proteins.
# - GO Cellular Component (CC): Maps subcellular localization to show where the virus hijacks host machinery.
# - KEGG: Maps the gene lists to well-established signaling and metabolic pathways.
dbs <- c("GO_Biological_Process_2023", 
         "GO_Molecular_Function_2023", 
         "GO_Cellular_Component_2023", 
         "KEGG_2021_Human")

# 2. Query the EnrichR API using the isolated H7N9-exclusive gene symbols.
# This statistically evaluates which biological concepts are significantly 
# over-represented in our specific viral signature compared to random chance.
enrich_up <- enrichr(unique_up_H7N9, dbs)
enrich_down <- enrichr(unique_down_H7N9, dbs)

# 3. Visualize Cellular Component (CC) for Downregulated genes.
# Identifying suppressed structural components often reveals which host barriers 
# or antigen presentation machinery the virus actively dismantles (e.g., cell surface).
plotEnrich(enrich_down[["GO_Cellular_Component_2023"]], 
           showTerms = 15, 
           numChar = 50, 
           y = "Count", 
           orderBy = "P.value") +
  ggtitle("GO Cellular Component: Downregulated uniquely in H7N9") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))

# 4. Visualize Biological Process (BP) for Downregulated genes.
# This complements the CC spatial data by showing exactly which functional 
# defense programs the virus is shutting down at those subcellular locations.
plotEnrich(enrich_down[["GO_Biological_Process_2023"]], 
           showTerms = 15, 
           numChar = 50, 
           y = "Count", 
           orderBy = "P.value") +
  ggtitle("GO Biological Process: Downregulated uniquely in H7N9") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))
```

# Volcano plots (all viruses)

```{r}
library(ggrepel)

volcano <- function(virus, time, n_labels = 10) {
  d <- res[[paste(virus, time, sep = "_")]]
  d$statut <- "NS"
  d$statut[is_deg(d) & d$log2FC > 0] <- "Up"
  d$statut[is_deg(d) & d$log2FC < 0] <- "Down"
  n_up <- sum(d$statut == "Up"); n_down <- sum(d$statut == "Down")
  d$statut <- factor(d$statut, levels = c("Up", "Down", "NS"),
                     labels = c(paste0("Up (", n_up, ")"), paste0("Down (", n_down, ")"), "NS"))
  
  # Colours (Up = red, Down = blue, NS = grey)
  cols <- setNames(c("red", "blue", "grey70"), levels(d$statut))
  
  top <- head(d[d$statut != "NS", ][order(d$pval[d$statut != "NS"]), ], n_labels)
  
  ggplot(d, aes(log2FC, -log10(pval), color = statut)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.2, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-FC_cut, FC_cut), linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(P_cut), linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_text_repel(data = top, aes(label = gene), color = "black", size = 3,
                    max.overlaps = 30, box.padding = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = cols, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "top",
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) +
    labs(title = paste0(virus, " vs Mock (", time, ")"),
         x = expression(log[2]~"Fold Change"), y = expression(-log[10]~italic(p)*"-value")) +
    # the same axes for all volcanoes -> allowing for comparison between viruses and over time
    coord_cartesian(xlim = x_lim, ylim = y_lim)
}

# Common axis limits, calculated from the 16 comparisons
x_lim <- range(sapply(res, function(d) range(d$log2FC, na.rm = TRUE)))
y_lim <- c(0, max(sapply(res, function(d) max(-log10(d$pval), na.rm = TRUE))))

# One volcano per virus and per time point (4 viruses x 4 time points = 16 figures)
for (v in viruses) {
  for (t in times) {
    p <- volcano(v, t)
    print(p)
    ggsave(paste0("figures/05_volcano_", v, "_", t, ".png"), p, width = 6, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
  }
}
```

```{r}
})))

# Différence de cinétique H7N9 vs H3N2 (somme des écarts sur les 4 temps)
tp <- c("03h", "07h", "12h", "24h")
diff_kin <- rowSums(abs(lfc[sig_H7N9, paste0("H7N9_", tp)] -
                          lfc[sig_H7N9, paste0("H3N2_", tp)]))

# Retirer les transcrits non annotés et garder le top 15
diff_kin <- diff_kin[!grepl("^(LOC|XLOC)", names(diff_kin))]
top_kin  <- names(sort(diff_kin, decreasing = TRUE))[1:15]
top_kin

# Vérifier que les gènes de ton panel existent dans le jeu de données
panel <- c("IFIH1", "DDX58", "IFNB1", "IL28A", "STAT1", "MX1", "IFIT1",
           "RSAD2", "IL6", "CXCL10", "PIGR", "CFH", "PDHA1")
panel[!panel %in% rownames(data_log)]   # gènes absents
```

```{r}
genes_cles <- intersect(c("IFNB1", "GBP7", "IL28B", "CXCL9", "C17", "IL29",
                          "IL28A", "CCL5", "IL6", "TNF", "IFIT1B", "SLC15A3","PPBP" ), rownames(expr))
if (length(genes_cles) > 0) {
  kin <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(res), function(nm) {
    d <- res[[nm]]
    data.frame(gene   = genes_cles,
               log2FC = d$log2FC[match(genes_cles, d$gene)],
               virus  = strsplit(nm, "_")[[1]][1],
               time   = strsplit(nm, "_")[[1]][2])
  }))
  p_kin <- ggplot(kin, aes(time, log2FC, color = virus, group = virus)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) + geom_point(size = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("H3N2" = "#377EB8", "H7N7" = "#FF7F00",
                                  "H7N9" = "#984EA3", "VN1203" = "#4DAF4A")) +
    facet_wrap(~ gene, scales = "free_y") +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(title = "Kinetics of key genes (log2FC vs mock)",
         x = "Time post-infection", y = "log2 Fold Change vs mock")
  
  print(p_kin)
  ggsave("figures/10_cinetique_genes_cles.png", p_kin, width = 10, height = 20)
} else {
  cat("Gènes clés non trouvés : les noms de lignes ne sont peut-être pas des symboles\n")
}

cat("\nTerminé ! Figures dans figures/, tableaux dans results/\n")
```
